messages.author: caa988883996a42b
messages.subject: OpenCR fiiting problem
parts:
Hi 
I am unable to run openCR, with my data, could you please inspect the issue. 
One issue I can guess "invalid factor level,NA generated= openCR doesn't allow to include sex as NA??
thanks and regards
Ujjwal

> fit1<-openCR.fit(CH2, type="JSSAsecrlCL", mask=msk, model=list(p~1,phi~t+sex,lambda~session), movementmodel="exponential") 
Error: cannot allocate vector of size 4.9 Gb
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In `[<-.factor`(`*tmp*`, thisvar, value = 0) :
  invalid factor level, NA generated
2: In matrix(unlist(indices), ncol = npar) :
  data length [10150272] is not a sub-multiple or multiple of the number of rows [2030055]

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: OpenCR fiiting problem
parts:
Hi Ujjwal

It's true that openCR.fit does not implement the 'hybrid mixture models' that allow you to include missing values for sex in secr.fit. That may be the whole of your problem - I don't know.

In general, I warn that openCR is not supported to the same level as secr, as I warned somewhere in the documentation. I would not be trying to fit a movement model or sex model, or even a spatial model, until everything else is sorted.

Cheers
Murray

messages.subject: Re: OpenCR fiiting problem
parts:
My Bayesian open population SCR package has a sampler for sex-specific parameters that allows missing values, but doesn't have as many other bells and whistles as Murray's package. It may or may not meet your needs. I think the maximum likelihood approach will start becoming computationally intractable once you start adding more random effects like this.

https://github.com/benaug/OpenPopSCR

messages.subject: Re: OpenCR fiiting problem
parts:
OpenPopSCR sounds like a good solution if it covers Ujjwal's case. Your point about MLE is well-taken, but I suspect the threshold of intractability is further out. The discrete random effect implied by a 2-part mixture model is easy to fit except for potential multimodality (I wonder if MCMC is completely robust to that). And sometimes sex differences are not as important as you might think.
Murray

messages.author: 2c49652a5796ed9c
messages.subject: Re: OpenCR fiiting problem
parts:
One thing I always forget to mention when directing someone to the Bayesian-based package is that they might need to run 20 chains or so to get an acceptable effective sample size for the dispersal sigma, so maybe I'm the one flirting with computational intractability! You can do them in parallel, though, if you have the resources. I haven't run into multimodality with unknown sexes, yet. I understand how this happens with completely latent finite mixtures, but don't see how it happens when they are partially observed and so there is no label switching.

Of the 3 data sets I've explored with the package so far, they've all had interesting sex-specific population dynamics and/or dispersal differences.

messages.subject: Re: OpenCR fiiting problem
parts: I take that back, with large sex differences in sigma, I've seen some multimodality in the sex-specific sigma as influential unknown sex individuals are updated from male to female and vice versa. I haven't seen this propagate to other parameters we care more about, though. This is fine except it complicates the decision about how to calculate the point estimate for sigma (posterior mode, mean, median, etc.)

messages.author: 2c49652a5796ed9c
messages.subject: Re: OpenCR fiiting problem
parts:
One other distinction between how sex is handled in openCR and OpenPopSCR may be the population growth model. Does openCR allow covariates on per capita recruitment? If so, what is the implied population growth model when that covariate is sex?

In OpenPopSCR, gamma^m and gamma^f are the per sex per capita recruitment rates--how many males per N and females per N are added to the population each year.  N^m_t= N^m_{t-1}*(phi^m+gamma^m) and N^f_t= N^f_{t-1}*(phi^f+gamma^f) with N^total_t= N^m_t +N^f_t. So you can estimate sex by year N and D, yearly sex ratio, and sex-specific and total population growth rate by inter-primary period.

messages.subject: Re: OpenCR fiiting problem
parts:
I screwed up the growth rate model

N^m_t =N^m_{t-1}*phi^m + N^total_{t-1} *gamma^m and N^f_t =N^f_{t-1}*phi^f+ N^total_{t-1} *gamma^f

not
N^m_{t-1}*(phi^m+gamma^m) and N^f_t= N^f_{t-1}*(phi^f+gamma^f)
# of recruits per sex is a function of total N, not sex-specific N.
